messages:
support-liz: @customer-jordan thanks, opening thread. Customer reporting intermittent 502s and TLS handshake failures to private Redwood endpoint in their VPC after a firewall change this morning. Reported start: ~08:15 UTC. They see OCSP timeouts and short-lived UDP drops.
customer-jordan: Observed from our app: lots of 502 and 522. curl shows TLS handshake: "tlsv1 alert unknown ca" sometimes, other times "connection reset by peer". Logs: `TLS handshake error: no shared cipher` and `OCSP fetch timeout`.
sre-ian: Can you paste the curl output and the exact gateway IPs? Also, did you recently change egress allowlists or NAT rules on the customer firewall? :eyes:
customer-jordan: Sure — gw: 10.8.2.5/32 (on our side). We pushed a tightened egress firewall at 08:10 that started dropping outbound UDP > ephemeral range except 443. No changes to IPsec config.
support-liz: Noted. deploy-bot: config_change applied by netops-ryan at 2026-03-17T08:09:47Z — firewall: tighten-egress-policy (#2451)
deploy-bot: rule summary: default-deny outbound, allow tcp:443,80, udp:53.
eng-infra-maya: This smells like NAT-T / UDP 4500 being blocked. IPsec NAT-T uses UDP 4500 for encapsulated ESP. If UDP 4500 or ESP (protocol 50) is blocked/filtered, rekey and keepalive packets can drop and cause intermittent handshake failures and connection resets.
sre-ian: Also check PMTU / fragmentation. If firewall drops ICMP or fragments, larger TLS records after initial handshake can fail. Ask them to run `ping -M do -s 1400 <peer>` and `traceroute --mtu` to check path MTU.
customer-jordan: Ran ping: packets > 1360 get no replies. `ping -s 1400` fails. ICMP blocked on egress by policy.
netops-ryan: We blocked ICMP intentionally as part of the tightened policy — can open ICMP only to the Redwood gateway for PMTU? We can add exceptions.
sre-ian: Two immediate actions to try:
1) Allow UDP 4500 and ESP (proto 50) on the egress policy to the Redwood peer IPs.
2) Temporarily allow ICMP (type: fragmentation-needed) or increase MTU clamp on the IPsec gateway to 1400 to avoid fragmentation.
support-liz: @netops-ryan can you add rules to allow UDP 4500 and ESP to the listed Redwood peer IPs and open ICMP for PMTU? If you can't do ESP (some firewalls don't support proto 50), at minimum allow UDP 4500 and set MTU clamp to 1400.
netops-ryan: Will do. Pushing changes now.
deploy-bot: firewall_rule_update applied by netops-ryan at 2026-03-17T08:22:03Z — allow udp:4500 to 52.45.12.200/32, open icmp type 3 code 4 to 52.45.12.200/32
customer-jordan: Re-tested after rule push. Curl now shows full handshake, OCSP lookups succeed. App errors dropped to near zero. :tada:
eng-infra-maya: For a durable fix, recommend:
- Add egress allowlist entries for OCSP/responder endpoints used by the CA (e.g., ocsp.int-x3.letsencrypt.org, ocsp.digicert.com) and CRL endpoints.
- Make MTU clamp on IPsec gw 1400
- Ensure anti-replay and keepalive intervals are compatible if there's aggressive NAT timeouts
- Add monitoring alert on rapid rekey failures and ESP drops
sre-ian: Also consider enabling UDP encapsulation keepalives and strict NAT-T handling on both sides. We'll document the suggested firewall profile in the customer runbook.
support-liz: Great — I'll update the ticket with the mitigation steps and ask customer to confirm for 24h. Thanks everyone.
customer-jordan: Confirming stable for 30m. Thank you all. :pray:
support-liz: Closing in 24h if stable. Escalation summary will be posted to the account thread and playbook updated.
